items.title: Runtime source authority is explicitly separated
items.statement: The core makes seglog authoritative, redb projected/read-optimized, and requested JSON/JSONL inspection-only; it also rejects loose JSON as canon. This is a clear authority boundary rather than an inferred one.

evidence.exact_quote: Storage keeps the orchestration source stack explicit: `event/source-of-truth` (`/source-of-truth`) aspects live in seglog, `projected/current-state/read-optimized` (`/current-state/read-optimized`) aspects live in redb, and `/inspection` export views are JSON/JSONL (`/JSONL`) only when the user requests them from UI surfaces such as Orchestrator. Loose JSON files are never the canonical source for these artifacts.

items.title: Operational identity is distinct from provider account identity
items.statement: Externally scoped target authority is not conflated with the provider account that executes an action; requested and effective operational identity are retained for audit.

evidence.exact_quote: Runtime records for side-effectful or externally-scoped actions include an `operational-identity` block distinct from provider account identity. The block records requested and effective operational refs, kind, selection reason, partial capability, target authority, and surface-specific scope so GitHub, registry, Kubernetes, remote-mode, and other externally scoped actions remain auditable.

items.title: Direct-record mutation controls disclose trust state
items.statement: The GUI-facing contract requires currentness, generation match, supersession, and actionability disclosure before mutation controls appear, which directly guards against a misleading projection-only state.

evidence.exact_quote: Any direct record view that allows action must display currentness, generation match, superseded yes/no, and actionable yes/no before surfacing mutation controls; `/dismiss` remains concern lifecycle action vocabulary and `/restore` remains recovery lineage vocabulary.

items.title: Concern undo preserves history
items.statement: Concern undo is explicitly modeled as compensating lineage rather than destructive history erasure.

evidence.exact_quote: A concern undo is a compensating follow-up record, not history erasure.

items.title: Historical search preserves focused-run context
items.statement: The navigation contract explicitly prevents silent run-focus jumps for historical results and assigns broad cross-object search to the appropriate consumers.

evidence.exact_quote: Search and navigation route through the broad object model. A narrow Source Control panel should not own richer cross-object search; those flows belong in Orchestrator / command-palette flows rather than side-panel SCM UI, and Historical results preserve run context so search does not create silent run-focus jumps.

items.title: Records and artifacts are explicitly distinct
items.statement: The storage model distinguishes canonical structured records from linked file/blob/renderable artifacts, preventing artifact views from silently becoming replacement sources.

evidence.exact_quote: Records and artifacts stay separate: a record is the canonical structured object in Ledger/export/search/routing (`/export/search/routing`), while an artifact is the file/blob/renderable (`/blob/renderable`) output linked from that record.

items.title: Canonical owner headings do not carry local requirements or acceptance oracles
items.statement: The core opens with consecutive canonical owner headings without bodies. The later recovery prose is broad and cannot establish which producer, consumer, invariant, or falsifiable acceptance oracle satisfies each named owner section.

evidence.exact_quote:
### Owner-first canonicalization order
### Shared governance/runtime record envelope

### Artifacts index exact indexed fields
### Lane cleanup lineage fields
### P5 runtime storage special recovery register

items.title: Snapshot payload has no typed, versioned, or privacy lifecycle contract
items.statement: The payload names sensitive identity, persona, invocation, option, and account-pressure data but does not define types, optionality, schema version, size limits, validation, field-level access, redaction, retention, deletion, or export treatment. Replaying or exposing a snapshot therefore has no deterministic privacy or compatibility boundary.

evidence.exact_quote: payloads must preserve `{ tool_name`, `invocation_summary`, and `options }`, plus `result_id`, requested/effective provider, requested/effective model, requested/effective account, requested_persona, effective_persona, permission_snapshot_id, account_switch_reason, account_pressure_episode, requirements_quality_report_ref, and the /chat/GUI disclosure

items.title: Route normalization omits input validation and authorization rules
items.statement: Raw command payloads can select projects, runs, records, artifacts, attempts, lanes, worktrees, filters, inspectors, and scroll targets, but the core does not define parsing limits, unknown-field behavior, identifier validation, cross-project authorization, target existence rules, or how ambiguous resolver output fails closed.

evidence.exact_quote: Surface-specific wrappers may stay user-facing, but raw payloads normalize into route-derived target and subject forms; `destination_surface`, `destination_tab`, `object_kind`, `object_id`, `record_id`, `artifact_id`, `attempt_id`, `lane_id`, `worktree_id`, `usage_event_ref`, `filter_payload`, `inspector_target`, `scroll_target`, and `focus_behavior` are canonical command routing fields.

items.title: Compatibility aliases have no executable migration mapping
items.statement: Aliases are declared searchable or subordinate, but no versioned alias-to-canonical mapping, collision precedence, case or Unicode normalization, telemetry, retirement threshold, downgrade behavior, or rejection rule is defined. Compatibility inputs can therefore persist as a parallel identity world despite the prohibition.

evidence.exact_quote: Snapshot vocabulary stays literal for compatibility: `{ tool_name, invocation_summary, options }`, Plans/interview-subagent-integration.md, and /interview-subagent-integration.md are preserved as searchable aliases while the canonical storage owner remains attempt and permission snapshot records.
Migration aliases stay explicit but subordinate.

items.title: Projection trust has no deterministic race-safe policy
items.statement: The core names projection states and says storage decides whether inspection, mutation, or export is permitted, but it supplies no freshness unit, thresholds, transition triggers, generation token, canonical-read barrier, revalidation validity window, or compare-and-swap rule. A projection may become stale between disclosure/revalidation and mutation, leaving a TOCTOU path to misleading GUI truth and unsafe writes.

evidence.exact_quote: Projection trust is operational: `projection_freshness` is the recency field and `projection_health` is the reliability/usability field, with states current, refreshing, stale, degraded, and unavailable. The base freshness/health model already carries `/health`; the missing requirement is `trust-state` operationalization, where storage decides when stale or degraded projections can be inspected, when canonical revalidation is required, and when mutation or export authority is withheld.

items.title: Lane and worktree lifecycle lacks a legal transition model
items.statement: Two vocabularies are presented for lane/worktree state without an explicit orthogonal-state model or total mapping. The core does not define legal transitions, initiating authority, preconditions, idempotency, concurrent cleanup versus restore behavior, tombstone semantics, or compensation when lane and worktree persistence diverge. Archive/remove and cleanup eligibility are destructive enough that this is a critical state-integrity gap.

evidence.exact_quote: Lane/worktree lifecycle keeps `baseline`, `active`, `suspect`, `restoring`, `retained`, `cleanup_eligible`, `archived`, `removed`, and `historical` as distinct states. `historical`, `archived`, `removed`, `retained`, and `cleanup_eligible` carry cross-surface meanings and must not collapse into a generic cleanup bucket.

Source Control uses a concrete worktree-first row posture: `live`, `dirty`, `conflict`, `orphaned`, `recovering`, `retained`, `archived`, and `removed`. The compact lifecycle vocabulary `baseline/active/suspect/restoring/retained/cleanup_eligible/archived/removed/historical` is a migration alias for those individually queryable states, not a collapsed generic worktree state.

items.title: Concern lifecycle orders dismissal after resolution despite conflicting semantics
items.statement: The declared linear lifecycle permits dismissal only after resolution, while dismissal is defined as rejecting or hiding actionable framing and can disagree with still-live corroborated evidence. The core does not state whether active or acknowledged concerns may be dismissed, whether resolved concerns can be dismissed, how reopen interacts with either state, or which transitions require new records. Consumers cannot implement a consistent state machine.

evidence.exact_quote: Concern lifecycle remains `active -> acknowledged -> resolved -> dismissed`; annotation examples may use `open -> addressed -> resolved`; wizard status distinguishes attention_required from blocked.

`dismissed` means the presentation was intentionally hidden or `/rejected` as actionable framing and requires rationale when it disagrees with corroborated or `/high-severity` evidence; `resolved` means the underlying truth changed and records `resolution_kind`.

items.title: Temporary concern projection has no cutover protocol
items.statement: The specification authorizes a temporary `finding_refs[]` representation until `node_concerns[]` exists but does not define the trigger, dual-read or dual-write interval, backfill, deduplication, canonical precedence, rollback, or behavior when one representation is only partially populated.

evidence.exact_quote: Short-term concern rendering may piggyback on `finding_refs[]` only until a minimal non-remediation `node_concerns[]` projection exists for node-level concern display.

items.title: Event-source authority lacks replay and corruption recovery semantics
items.statement: Seglog is correctly made authoritative, but the core does not define event ordering, duplicate suppression, idempotent projector application, snapshot/checkpoint consistency, crash boundaries, corrupt or truncated tail handling, schema upgrades during replay, projector rebuild verification, or rollback after a bad projection. Replayability is claimed without a falsifiable recovery algorithm.

evidence.exact_quote: Runtime coordination/audit cannot claim both file-based canon and event-sourced canon as primary authority. Storage treats file-based canon as export/inspection mirror material and event-sourced canon as the seglog/source-of-truth path for replayable runtime coordination/audit.

items.title: Recovery record fields do not define recovery execution
items.statement: The record enumerates useful metadata but not recovery states, actor authority, safe-point validity, locks, generation checks, idempotency key, timeout and cancellation, partial-result semantics, compensation, retry ceiling, or the acceptance oracle proving restored canonical and projected state agree.

evidence.exact_quote: Recovery records include `recovery kind`, `safe-point restore`, `restart reconciliation`, `blocked prerequisite resolution`, `lane/worktree restore`, `target scope refs`, `trigger reason`, `preconditions`, `result`, `resulting attempt/run linkage`, and `affected concern refs`.

items.title: Export manifests omit atomicity, privacy, offline, and scale behavior
items.statement: The manifest taxonomy is strong, but no consistent-cut algorithm, authorization model, redaction policy, retention/deletion rule, encryption requirement, maximum size, pagination/streaming/backpressure contract, cancellation, retry/resume behavior, partial-bundle marker, or network-loss recovery is specified. A bundle can therefore be internally inconsistent, leak sensitive identity data, or appear complete after partial failure.

evidence.exact_quote: Export contracts define canonical manifests before surface views: Orchestrator exports, Ledger/Usage CSV/JSON, thread exports, artifact bundles, record bundles, and general app exports distinguish view-shaped exports from record-shaped bundles. The canonical manifest records export family, scope, canonical IDs/refs, included records/artifacts/references, artifact path rules, superseded/removed/historical backing-object disclosure, trust-state, and whether view re-query or canonical revalidation happened; CSV and JSON are serializations, not source-of-truth.

items.title: Shared record families are named without enforceable schemas
items.statement: The governance envelope and canonical object bundle list fields but do not define a schema version, discriminant-to-required-field matrix, key uniqueness, cardinality, nullability, referential constraints, temporal invariants, unknown-field policy, or subtype evolution rules. Producers can emit structurally incompatible records while all claiming conformance to the same template.

evidence.exact_quote: Governance storage uses one `governance-record` template for concern, review, promotion, corroboration, graph-patch, and recovery records (`/review/promotion/corroboration/graph-patch/recovery`). That template carries the shared envelope, lineage refs, status, actor identity, timing, evidence refs, artifact refs, source refs, and `/contracts` linkage so those durable records do not emerge ad hoc per surface.

Runtime storage is SSOT for record-shaped state, not for every consumer surface. The canonical family bundle includes `{project`, `run`, `seam`, `package`, `node`, `attempt`, `lane`, `promotion`, `review`, `resolution_thread}`

items.title: Large-run queryability has no capacity or performance contract
items.statement: The core identifies high-cardinality records and requires separate queryability but supplies no index definitions, sort stability, cursor semantics, result caps, retention or compaction policy, cardinality ceilings, latency/service objectives, memory budget, or degradation/backpressure behavior.

evidence.exact_quote: Large-run density is a real-world storage concern: many active and historical concerns, corroboration `/review/promotion/recovery` records, retained lanes, and cleanup-eligible lanes/worktrees (`/worktrees`) must remain separately queryable instead of collapsing into one graph-only summary.

items.title: Receipt joins lack referential, causal, and privacy invariants
items.statement: Receipt, usage, and provider references are distinguished, but there is no uniqueness scope, foreign-key behavior, causal ordering, duplicate resolution, missing/delayed event policy, cross-project authorization check, actor/account redaction rule, retention boundary, or test for coherent joining. Historical pivots may resolve to the wrong project or reveal sensitive attribution.

evidence.exact_quote: Cross-surface receipt records require `project_id`, actor refs, `created_at_utc`, and `usage_event_ref` whenever a surface may pivot historically or across projects. `usage_event_ref` and `usage_event_id` are receipt and Usage/docs join fields, while `provider_attempt_ref` joins provider traces; downstream surfaces must join them coherently instead of substituting one for the other.

items.title: Execution identity contains duplicate spellings without precedence
items.statement: The attempt/session field list mixes `actor-role` with `actor_role`, name forms with ID forms, legacy context with canonical context, and requested/effective disclosure without defining canonical keys, precedence, equivalence, optionality, or privacy filtering. Concurrent or mixed-version producers can persist conflicting identities and consumers have no deterministic winner.

evidence.exact_quote: They include execution_unit_context, optional decomposition_context and view_context for legacy prompt or UI help, action-family, execution_role, operational_identity, actor-aware /actor-snapshot, actor-role, actor_role, run-level, feature_seam, feature_seam_id, work_package, work_package_id, package-governance, seam-promotion, execution-context, selected_worktree_id, selected_repo_id, workspace_ref, mutation_capable, side-effect, and provider_attempt_ref.

items.title: Legacy event ingestion has no ordering or downgrade contract
items.statement: Many legacy event forms may be ingested, but no per-version decoder, canonical event mapping, ordering key, duplicate policy, unknown-event quarantine, partial-batch behavior, downgrade behavior, or audit oracle is defined. A mixed old/new stream can produce divergent attempt and blocked projections.

evidence.exact_quote: Storage may ingest `run.tier_started`, `run.tier_completed`, `run.persona_stage_changed`, `tier_runtime_record`, `tier_id`, `tier_type`, `tier-era`, `tier-start`, `tier-boundary`, `PuppetMasterEvent`, `PuppetMasterEvent::*`, `PuppetMasterEvent::Output`, `PuppetMasterEvent::TierChanged`, `PuppetMasterEvent::IterationStart`, `PuppetMasterEvent::EvidenceStored`, `PuppetMasterEvent::UserInteractionRequired`, `TierChanged`, `IterationStart`, `EvidenceStored`, and `UserInteractionRequired` as migration inputs, but canonical runtime-core records persist node/attempt/package/seam/lane identity.

items.title: Attention escalation lacks thresholds and deduplication
items.statement: Escalation depends on severity and elapsed time, but the core defines neither severity mapping nor elapsed-time thresholds, clock source, reset rules, deduplication, quiet-hours interaction, notification permission, retry behavior, or de-escalation. Consumers can produce contradictory or noisy blocked truth.

evidence.exact_quote: Attention delivery keeps `/in-app` advisory concerns distinct from seam-blocking weak-integration concerns. `/minor` advisory rows stay local or in-app, while seam-blocking concerns with no progress can escalate to blocked surfaces and system notification according to severity and elapsed time.

items.title: Allowed actions are not bound to authorization or record generation
items.statement: Displaying currentness and an action list is not sufficient for safe mutation. The core does not bind `allowed_action_ids` to actor identity, permission snapshot, record generation, expiry, nonce/idempotency key, or a server-side compare-and-swap at execution. Stale or replayed UI state can authorize a destructive action after conditions change.

evidence.exact_quote: Any direct record view that allows action must display currentness, generation match, superseded yes/no, and actionable yes/no before surfacing mutation controls
`allowed_action_ids` and `allowed_action_ids[]` identify permitted direct actions

items.title: Account pressure episodes lack transition and data-lifecycle invariants
items.statement: The episode fields and statuses are named, but legal transitions, timestamp ordering, uniqueness, overlapping episodes, signal update precedence, invalidation authority, terminal-state reopening, retention, redaction, and account/project access rules are absent. Conflicting signals can leave pressure state permanently active or expose account-level operational data.

evidence.exact_quote: Account pressure episodes are durable attribution records, not UI-only account hints. `account_pressure_episode` carries `episode_id`, `project_id`, `provider_id`, `account_id`, `execution_role?`, `source_kind`, `signal_confidence`, `pressure_kind`, `projected_remaining?`, `reset_at?`, `started_at_utc`, `updated_at_utc`, `ended_at_utc?`, and `status`; status values are `active | cooled_down | resolved | invalidated`, with `cooled_down` preserved as a queryable state rather than flattened into resolved.

items.title: UI-facing storage truth has no accessibility or localization contract
items.statement: The core reaches into user copy/help and mandates visible currentness/actionability, but it does not define locale-independent enum values versus localized labels, fallback locale, Unicode/search normalization, accessible names/descriptions, non-color state semantics, announcement of trust changes, focus behavior, or keyboard-operable recovery actions. Native consumers can render the same canonical state inconsistently or misleadingly for assistive-technology and non-English users.

evidence.exact_quote: Legacy `tier` wording that remains in storage, contracts, `user-copy`, or `/help` text is both a data-model risk and a user-copy/help migration risk.
Any direct record view that allows action must display currentness, generation match, superseded yes/no, and actionable yes/no before surfacing mutation controls

items.title: Observability and acceptance oracles are underspecified
items.statement: Tool analytics cover latency, success, and error, and runtime-era actions require verification/routing coverage, but the core does not define correlation IDs across events/receipts/projections, error taxonomy, projection lag and replay metrics, health thresholds, alert ownership, audit sampling, structured failure fields, or executable acceptance predicates. Operational support cannot distinguish a delayed projector from missing or corrupt canonical data.

evidence.exact_quote: Tool events (`tool.invoked`) keep `tool_name`, `run_id`, optional `thread_id`, latency, success, and error as analytics fields, but storage joins them through the same attempt/receipt/usage/artifact attribution packet instead of a separate tool-only identity world.
`/verification/routing` coverage is required for runtime-era actions and records before `/matrix/gate` decisions can claim complete authority.

items.title: Externally scoped actions omit ambiguous network-outcome recovery
items.statement: Operational identity makes the target auditable, but there is no contract for offline initiation, connect and read timeouts, retryability, idempotency tokens, remote-side success with local receipt failure, reconciliation after reconnect, partial capability changes, or compensating action. GitHub, registry, Kubernetes, and remote-mode operations can have unknown completion status.

evidence.exact_quote: The block records requested and effective operational refs, kind, selection reason, partial capability, target authority, and surface-specific scope so GitHub, registry, Kubernetes, remote-mode, and other externally scoped actions remain auditable.

items.title: Generated-artifact materialization has no partial-failure state
items.statement: A single subject-open contract is required across staged/generated state, later filesystem materialization, and backing-document assignment, but the core does not define intermediate states, atomic binding, missing-path behavior, rename/move races, content/hash verification, retry, rollback, or how consumers open a record when materialization fails.

evidence.exact_quote: The planning/UI docs may describe staged/generated flows, but storage owns one canonical subject-open contract for the first-class staged/generated artifact, later filesystem path materialization, and backing-document assignment.

dimension_assessments.summary: Owner headings, record envelopes, receipt joins, and materialization contracts do not enumerate complete producer/consumer responsibilities or failure behavior.
Lane/worktree, concern, and account-pressure lifecycles lack total legal transition models, and concern dismissal semantics conflict with the stated linear order.
Projection revalidation, event replay, and direct-action authorization lack generation-bound atomicity and compare-and-swap behavior.
Temporary projection migration, replay, recovery, exports, external operations, and filesystem materialization have no complete partial-result model.
The core records recovery intent but omits executable idempotency, compensation, retry, rollback, and consistency-verification contracts.
Source and operational identity boundaries are explicitly strong, but route execution, recovery, export, and direct actions are not bound to actor authorization and record generation.
Snapshots, exports, receipts, execution identities, account-pressure episodes, and remote operational refs lack retention, deletion, redaction, encryption, and access-control rules.
Raw route payloads and legacy aliases/events do not have fail-closed validation, decoding, collision, or quarantine behavior.

Currentness disclosure is explicitly required, but trust-state thresholds, concern transitions, escalation rules, and action execution remain underspecified and can make displayed actionability stale or contradictory.
Exports, external side effects, and later filesystem materialization omit offline, timeout, reconnect, resume, and ambiguous-outcome reconciliation.
Bundle export and large-run query requirements lack cardinality ceilings, paging, streaming, backpressure, resource budgets, and performance objectives.
UI-facing trust and mutation states have no assistive semantics, announcements, keyboard/focus behavior, or non-color representation contract.
Searchable aliases and user-facing state vocabulary lack locale-independent key versus localized-label separation, Unicode normalization, and fallback behavior.
Alias search, temporary concern projection, and legacy event ingestion lack versioned mapping, cutover, backfill, collision, retirement, and downgrade contracts.
Analytics fields exist, but correlation, projector lag/replay health, structured error taxonomy, thresholds, and support ownership are missing.
Archive/remove, restore, dismiss, graph patch, and other direct mutations lack generation-bound authorization, idempotency, compensation, and race-safe execution.
The core names owner headings, consumer documents, compatibility aliases, shared account/runtime contracts, and materialization ownership without locally testable handoff schemas or closure evidence.
Named states, recovery fields, replayability, export trust, escalation, and verification coverage are not paired with executable predicates and failure oracles.

Duplicate spellings, broad alias sets, prose-only record lists, and unspecified observability make the blast radius of mixed-version producers and unseen consumers unknowable within this blind window.
